Influence Capability

Source: R/centrality-batch68.R
centrality_influence_capability.Rd

Influence capability (IC; Wang et al. 2017) adds a position term from the k-shell decomposition and a neighborhood term, each divided by its total and weighted by the entropy weight method: $$IC(i) = w_1 \frac{ICP(i)}{\sum_l ICP(l)} + w_2 \frac{ICN(i)}{\sum_l ICN(l)}, \qquad ICP(i) = k_i - |\Gamma(i)| + \sum_{j \in \Gamma(i)} \tfrac{2}{\pi} \arctan Iter(j)^{1/3}, \qquad ICN(i) = \sum_{j \in N(i)} \sum_{l \in N(j)} k_l,$$ with \(k\) the degree, \(Iter(j)\) the iteration of the k-shell decomposition in which \(j\) is removed, counted across the shells from 1, \(\Gamma(i)\) the neighbors of \(i\) removed in an earlier iteration, and \(w_x = (1 - H_x) / (2 - H_1 - H_2)\), \(H_x\) the entropy of the shares of attribute \(x\) divided by \(\ln n\).

Usage

centrality_influence_capability(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality, such as normalized.

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The measure is computed on the simple undirected skeleton of the network, so direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. An iteration removes at once every remaining node whose degree is at most the current level, which starts at 1; a check that removes nothing raises the level and does not count. An isolated node is removed in the first iteration, with the leaves. The source's equation (4) weights "normalized" attributes without saying how; they are divided by their totals, the normalisation of its equation (5) (owner decision 2026-11-26). Its equation (7) is printed with a leading minus sign, which its positive weights rule out. When both attributes take one value at every node, as on a regular network, equation (7) is 0/0; the weights are then one half each, which does not change the scores. The implementation reproduces the iteration numbers, position terms and neighborhood terms printed in the source's worked example, the 14 rank groups of the IC column of its Table 2, the ranking of its Table 1 (once three labels of its Fig. 3, which the table numbers differently, are exchanged), and the monotonicity of its Table 3 on the dolphins network (0.9958) and the karate club (0.9542, which is also the largest value an exact structural measure can reach there). The eight entropy weights the source prints for these four networks do not follow from its equations (they differ by 0.003 to 0.042); no printed ranking depends on them. On a network without edges equation (5) is 0/0, and the measure warns (class cograph_undefined_measure) and returns NA. On four test networks the score ranks nodes closest to centrality_lhc (mean Kendall correlation 0.95) and eskh (0.93); with the degree the correlation is 0.79 to 0.91. normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Wang, Z., Du, C., Fan, J. and Xing, Y. (2017). Ranking influential nodes in social networks based on node position and neighborhood. Neurocomputing, 260, 466-477. doi:10.1016/j.neucom.2017.04.064 .

See also

centrality_coreness, centrality_ks_if, centrality_degree, centrality.

Examples

centrality_influence_capability(regulation_net)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#> 0.09280429 0.10849957 0.12491403 0.10347724 0.09148043 0.09323724 0.07968034 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#> 0.09756676 0.11008191 0.09825819
